note: Fixture verification markers, one per provider. fixtureVerified true means this provider ships a frozen redacted sample whose parser test passes, so the parser is proven to read a real shaped response offline. This is NOT the honesty verification label in provider_specs, which stays UNVERIFIED for every provider whose interface the vendor does not officially publish. A fixture can be trusted while the interface behind it is still unofficial. Providers are added here one at a time as their fixture test passes.

claude.reason: The statusline payload is a shape Anthropic publishes, and the frozen fixture parses to the two windows the documentation states. A separate sanitized live capture proves the native desktop OAuth reader observed both windows on 2026-09-01. The TypeScript connector still accepts only the statusline shape, and the live OAuth interface remains internal, so the honesty label stays UNVERIFIED.

openrouter.reason: The credits response is a documented OpenRouter API shape, and the frozen fixture parses to one credits meter reading 62.35 percent from the two money figures, so the parser is fixture verified. The honesty label stays UNVERIFIED because a fixture proves the parser, not the account behind it.

codex.reason: The usage response was read from the personal Codex account on 2026-09-01 and reduced to the percentage, window length, and reset duration. The captured fixture parses to the one window the provider returned. The honesty label stays UNVERIFIED because the endpoint is internal and OpenAI publishes nothing about it.

antigravity.reason: The quota summary was read from the local Antigravity account on 2026-09-01 and reduced to closed pool names, window names, remaining fractions, and reset durations. The captured fixture parses both Gemini windows while leaving the third party pool alone. The honesty label stays UNVERIFIED because the endpoint is internal and Google publishes nothing about it.

gemini_cli.reason: The official Gemini CLI source defines the private quota bucket response. The frozen source derived fixture parses both model buckets and matches the shipped Rust collector, while the interface remains internal and UNVERIFIED.

opencode.reason: Left UNVERIFIED on purpose: the evidence is too thin for a trustworthy fixture. OpenCode publishes no usage interface at all, so the only source is the HTML of a logged in workspace page, and any fixture is a snapshot of a layout rather than a contract. The parser reads the frozen page correctly, but a passing scrape proves only that one frozen layout still parses, not that the provider exposes anything stable, so it is not marked fixture verified. This matches the connector's own labels: authenticated-scrape, automationRisk high.

grok.reason: The official Grok CLI source defines the billing response and request contract. The frozen source derived fixture parses the weekly credit window and the optional monthly on demand cap. This proves the offline collection path, while the interface remains internal and UNVERIFIED.

kimi.reason: The official Kimi CLI source defines the usage response and its provider defined windows. The frozen source derived fixture parses the weekly summary and five hour limit. This proves the offline collection path, while the interface remains internal and UNVERIFIED.
